title: Common-stage descent of the explicit adjunction and its coherence
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, and an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ [def-pur-conventions]. Let $X,Y$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes and $f:X\to Y$ smooth separated of pure relative dimension $d\geq0$ [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Write $\mathcal C_T(\Lambda)=\Dctf(T,\Lambda)$ for the bounded constructible finite-Tor pro-etale condensed-module category [sk-def-sfb-constructible], $F_{f,\Lambda}=Rf_{!,\Lambda}$, $G_{f,\Lambda}=f^!_\Lambda$ with its specified restricted adjunction $F_{f,\Lambda}\dashv G_{f,\Lambda}$ and counit $\varepsilon_{f,\Lambda}$ [sk-thm-existence], and $J_{f,\Lambda}=f^*_\Lambda(-)(d)[2d]$ with the Tate twists of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed].

For every finite $E\subset\Qlb$, suppose given the $E$-linear adjunction $F_{f,E}\dashv J_{f,E}$ obtained from the integral tower Hom bijections by scalar localization, with its localized integration counit $t_E$. Assume their Hom bijections, units and counits are compatible with finite coefficient-field inclusions using the transitive comparisons of [sk-lem-sp-field-extension]. Assume also that their counit-preserving purity comparisons with $G_{f,E}$ satisfy the finite-stage composition and Cartesian base-change equations. Use the ordinary-category two-colimit equivalence and Hom colimit of [sk-thm-sfb-qlbar-two-colimit], the comparison of ambient $R\bar f_*j_!$ with scalar extension $E\to\Qlb$ [det-prop-scalar-six-compact-support], and the pullback and twist comparisons [det-prop-scalar-six-pullback, sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients].

Then, for any $M\in\mathcal C_X(\Qlb)$ and $K\in\mathcal C_Y(\Qlb)$, choosing representatives $M_E,K_E$ over one finite $E$ gives a presentation-independent natural bijection
$$\operatorname{Hom}(F_{f,\Qlb}M,K)\simeq\varinjlim_{F\supset E}\operatorname{Hom}(F_{f,F}M_F,K_F)\simeq\varinjlim_{F\supset E}\operatorname{Hom}(M_F,J_{f,F}K_F)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(M,J_{f,\Qlb}K).$$
It defines $F_{f,\Qlb}\dashv J_{f,\Qlb}$ with counit the common-stage image of $t_E$, including its affine-line integration normalization. Its counit-preserving comparison with $G_{f,\Qlb}$ is the common-stage image of the given finite-field purity maps. The composition and Cartesian base-change identities hold as equalities of actual morphisms in the condensed categories. For any coefficient transition between these rational stages and $\Qlb$, the coefficient mate computed for the fixed $G_{f,\Lambda}$ is the conjugate of the explicit-adjoint mate by the counit-preserving comparisons, with the exact conjugation and coefficient-composition equations of [det-sp-unique-adjoint-coefficients]. Thus the coefficient equations refer to the originally specified exceptional adjoints as well as the common-stage explicit adjoints.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-raw-condensed-rational-adjunction-comparison] to each finite field and each finite inclusion. Its $R,u,v,\tau$ identify the given raw localized Hom bijections with the actual condensed ones, and the detailed Tate twists with the condensed lines, preserving the specified $a,b$, units, counits and scalar associators. Its hypotheses are precisely the integral-localized adjunction and the raw transitive comparisons assumed here; condensed compatibility is its conclusion. In what follows $J$ still means the twist of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed], realized by $v$, not a replacement twist. Write $T^W_{L/E}$ for ordinary condensed scalar extension and $T^W_E=T^W_{\Qlb/E}$. The compact-support theorem gives $b_E:T^Y_EF_{f,E}\simeq F_{f,\Qlb}T^X_E$ for the actual compactification composite. Pullback comparison, tensor reassociation and the twist line give $a_E:T^X_EJ_{f,E}\simeq J_{f,\Qlb}T^Y_E$. On a cover with compatible Kummer roots $\zeta_n$, the twist comparison sends $\zeta\otimes e$ to the same root times $e$; its colimit is the condensed $\Qlb$ line. Tensor $d$ times and shift $[2d]$. The monoidal comparison theorem, also for identity topoi with coefficient maps, gives associator, unitor and pullback-composition compatibility. These $a_E,b_E$ identify the endpoints of the outer Hom colimits.

source.place: Hom-colimit construction and independence/naturality paragraph; expanded with counit and mate calculations

proof.text: By the ordinary-category two-colimit theorem, choose $M_E,K_E$ and isomorphisms $T^X_EM_E\simeq M$, $T^Y_EK_E\simeq K$, after putting their two initial fields in a finite compositum. Its Hom formula at $r=0$, applied to $(F_{f,E}M_E,K_E)$ on $Y$ and $(M_E,J_{f,E}K_E)$ on $X$, together with Step 1, gives the two outer bijections in the statement. These are Hom sets in the full condensed constructible categories. The finite-diagram descent lemma applies to these very categories through that theorem, and will be used to lift changes of representatives and their inverse equations.

source.place: Hom-colimit construction and independence/naturality paragraph; expanded with counit and mate calculations

proof.text: Let $\alpha_L$ be the assumed finite-field adjunction bijection at $L\supset E$. On the middle colimits define $[L,h]\mapsto[L,\alpha_L(h)]$ and $[L,v]\mapsto[L,\alpha_L^{-1}(v)]$. The raw compatibility in the hypothesis, transported to the specified condensed comparisons by [lem-pur-raw-condensed-rational-adjunction-comparison], says exactly that applying either formula and then extending $L$ to $L'$ equals extending first and applying the formula at $L'$, under $a,b$. Equal representatives therefore have equal images, and the two composites are $[L,h]\mapsto[L,h]$ and $[L,v]\mapsto[L,v]$. Conjugate this bijection by the two outer bijections of Step 2 to define $\alpha_{\Qlb}$.

source.place: Hom-colimit construction and independence/naturality paragraph; expanded with counit and mate calculations

proof.text:
For different presentations choose a common finite $L$ on which the identifying isomorphisms $u:M_L\simeq\widetilde M_L$, $v:K_L\simeq\widetilde K_L$ and their inverses are defined, and enlarge once more so both inverse equations hold. This is the finite-diagram descent assertion, not faithfulness of scalar extension at a fixed stage. The arrow $h$ changes to $v\circ h\circ F_{f,L}(u^{-1})$. Finite-stage naturality gives
$$\alpha_L(v\circ h\circ F_{f,L}(u^{-1}))=J_{f,L}(v)\circ\alpha_L(h)\circ u^{-1}.$$
The outer identifications change by precisely these endpoint conjugations. Thus the resulting actual arrow is unchanged. The transition compatibility in Step 3 makes the argument independent of the larger $L$.

source.place: Hom-colimit construction and independence/naturality paragraph; expanded with counit and mate calculations

proof.text:
For actual arrows $u:M'\to M$ and $v:K\to K'$, choose a common finite presentation of these arrows and any $h:F_{f,\Qlb}M\to K$ by finite-diagram descent. Finite-stage naturality is the identity
$$\alpha_L(v_L\circ h_L\circ F_{f,L}(u_L))=J_{f,L}(v_L)\circ\alpha_L(h_L)\circ u_L.$$
Taking its image in the two Hom colimits gives the same identity for $\alpha_{\Qlb}$. This proves naturality for all arrows, including arrows not defined over the original $E$.

source.place: Hom-colimit construction and independence/naturality paragraph; expanded with counit and mate calculations

proof.text:
Apply the natural-bijection adjunction theorem to $\alpha_{\Qlb}$. It gives $F_{f,\Qlb}\dashv J_{f,\Qlb}$, with
$$\eta_M=\alpha_{\Qlb}(1_{F_{f,\Qlb}M}),\qquad t_K=\alpha_{\Qlb}^{-1}(1_{J_{f,\Qlb}K}),$$
and gives the triangle identities and both transpose formulas. In particular the counit here is determined by this Hom bijection, not chosen afterwards.

source.place: Hom-colimit construction and independence/naturality paragraph; expanded with counit and mate calculations

proof.text:
Evaluate those formulas on representatives. With the comparisons from Step 1 the resulting identities are
$$t_{T^Y_EK_E}\circ F_{f,\Qlb}(a_{E,K_E})=T^Y_E(t_{E,K_E})\circ b_{E,J_{f,E}K_E}^{-1},$$
$$\eta_{T^X_EM_E}=J_{f,\Qlb}(b_{E,M_E})\circ a_{E,F_{f,E}M_E}\circ T^X_E(\eta_{E,M_E}).$$
Indeed the identities defining these transposes are represented by the finite-stage identities, and Step 3 applies $\alpha_E$ or its inverse to them. These formulas identify both adjunction maps with their finite-stage images. For the affine-line structure map and the coefficient-unit input, the first formula is the scalar image of the assumed localized normalized integration $t_E$; the twist comparison fixes the same $\zeta$. Hence its normalization is retained.

source.place: Hom-colimit construction and independence/naturality paragraph; expanded with counit and mate calculations

proof.text: The originally specified $G_{f,\Qlb}$ is a right adjoint on these same full constructible categories, by the restriction clause of [sk-thm-existence]. Apply uniqueness of right adjoints to obtain $\gamma_{\Qlb}:G_{f,\Qlb}\simeq J_{f,\Qlb}$, characterized by $t\circ F_{f,\Qlb}(\gamma_{\Qlb})=\varepsilon_{f,\Qlb}$. Put $\delta_{\Qlb}=\gamma_{\Qlb}^{-1}$. Likewise let $\gamma_E=\delta_E^{-1}$ for each given finite-stage purity comparison. Thus $\delta_{\Qlb}:J_{f,\Qlb}\simeq G_{f,\Qlb}$ preserves the counit exactly.

source.place: Hom-colimit construction and independence/naturality paragraph; expanded with counit and mate calculations

proof.text:
For a rational transition $0\to1$, finite-to-finite or finite-to-$\Qlb$, let $c_G$ be the $G_1$-transpose of $T^Y(\varepsilon_0)\circ b(G_0)^{-1}$, and define $c_J$ using $t$. Step 7, or the finite-stage identity transported by [lem-pur-raw-condensed-rational-adjunction-comparison], gives $c_J=a$. To check the claimed conjugation take $F_1$ and then $t_1$. Counit compatibility and the mate equation give
$$t_1F_1(\gamma_1c_GT^X\delta_0)=\varepsilon_1F_1(c_G)F_1(T^X\delta_0)=T^Y(\varepsilon_0)b(G_0)^{-1}F_1(T^X\delta_0)=T^Y(\varepsilon_0F_0\delta_0)b(J_0)^{-1}=T^Y(t_0)b(J_0)^{-1}.$$
The penultimate equality is naturality of $b$. This is the transpose defining $c_J$, so injectivity of the adjunction bijection gives $c_J=\gamma_1c_GT^X(\delta_0)$. Equivalently $c_G T^X(\delta_0)=\delta_1a$, so $c_G$ is invertible. This is the exact common-stage meaning of the given finite purity map when its target is the originally specified exceptional adjoint.

source.place: Hom-colimit construction and independence/naturality paragraph; expanded with counit and mate calculations

proof.text:
For $0\to1\to2$, the explicit comparisons satisfy
$$J_2(s^Y_K)\circ c_{J,12}(T^Y_{01}K)\circ T^X_{12}(c_{J,01}(K))=c_{J,02}(K)\circ s^X_{J_0K},$$
where $s$ denotes scalar associators: for finite fields this is the raw transitivity transported with the actual scalar associators by [lem-pur-raw-condensed-rational-adjunction-comparison]; if stage 2 is $\Qlb$, then $c_{J,12}=a_1$ and $c_{J,02}=a_0$ by Step 7, and $c_{J,01}=a^c_{01}$ is the condensed comparison of Step 1, so all three are condensed pullback, tensor and twist scalar comparisons. The equation is then the coefficient-composition compatibility of the pullback comparisons in clause 3 of [det-prop-scalar-six-pullback], the monoidality of the composed scalar pullbacks in [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons] for the tensor factor, and the composition of the twist transitions $E_X(1)\to F_X(1)\to\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell,X}(1)$ of [sk-def-sp-tate-twist], compatible with pullback by [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients] (the same Kummer roots $\zeta_n$ at each stage); it is not the raw finite transitivity. Substitute $c_{G,ij}=\delta_j c_{J,ij}T^X_{ij}(\gamma_i)$ from Step 9. The adjacent $T^X_{12}(\gamma_1)$ and $T^X_{12}(\delta_1)$ cancel; naturality moves $\delta_2$ across $J_2(s^Y_K)$ and moves $\gamma_0$ across $s^X$. The result is exactly the displayed equation with $J,c_J$ replaced by $G,c_G$, with the same scalar associators. Identity transitions give $c_J=1$ and then $c_G=1$.

proof.text: The actual geometric comparisons also have the required representatives. Pullback composition and its tensor/twist factors commute with scalar extension by the monoidal comparison theorem and Step 1; for a Cartesian square use the scalar/pullback square-coherence statement. Compact-support composition is covered by the composition-compatible compact-support comparison. For compact-support base change, compute on a compactification: proper direct-image exchange followed by open-extension exchange. The scalar/geometric rectangle gives the proper factor. For the open factor apply the generic four-open-adjunction cube lemma: the condensed open-square theorem identifies the exchange by its prescribed open-unit transpose; the derived open-scalar isomorphism is the conjugate of scalar restriction/inverse image; and scalar/pullback square coherence is precisely the required cube. Thus that lemma gives the open scalar/exchange square for the present condensed rings, with no appeal to the constant-etale open-exchange theorem. Pasting these two squares gives the compact-support scalar/exchange square. The generic mate-pasting theorem then identifies the specified exceptional composition and base-change comparisons under $c_G$. All hypotheses concern ordinary module-derived functors and their actual unit/counit maps; the input constructible complexes lie in their domains. No arbitrary endpoint isomorphism replaces a specified geometric comparison.

source.place: Hom-colimit construction and independence/naturality paragraph; expanded with counit and mate calculations

proof.text: For composable smooth $f,g$, take the finite-stage composition equation in the hypothesis, including its specified twisted-pullback compositor, the two purity maps, and the counit-normalized exceptional compositor. The bridge of Step 1 identifies the finite explicit adjunctions and their counits; hence uniqueness in Step 8 identifies their counit-preserving purity maps with those in the hypothesis. Represent the input over $E$; all intermediate objects and arrows are the finite expressions over that same field after the comparisons of Steps 1, 9 and 11. Each side therefore represents the image of the same finite-stage morphism. For a Cartesian square do the same with its input and its two pullbacks: the finite-stage base-change equation is an equality in the category on the upper-left scheme, and Step 11 identifies every comparison occurring in its two paths. Its scalar image is thus the requested equality. A change of input representative or an enlargement of $E$ has no effect by Steps 3–5 and 10. These are equalities in the ordinary Hom sets of the condensed categories by the two-colimit Hom formula, not only equalities of isomorphism classes or of cohomology groups.
